title: 10 or 100 More and Less Worksheets
intro: Teach changes of ten or one hundred using place-value units.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Add or remove a tens rod or a hundreds flat. Show any regrouping instead of changing one digit mechanically.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

346 + 10 = 356; 346 − 10 = 336
346 + 100 = 446; 346 − 100 = 246

Use bundles or place-value blocks to show the change. Say the value of the group you add or remove before writing the new number.

Ask your student

What exchange is needed when we cross a hundred or a thousand?

If your student needs help

If a digit-only rule fails, rebuild the number and carry out the change with units.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet has four questions: one each for 10 more, 10 less, 100 more, and 100 less. Starting numbers range from 100 through 900, with answers from 0 through 1000. A particular set does not guarantee a regrouping case, zero, or 1000.
